items.title: Alaska prosecutor confirms criminal probe into ballot spoiler plot
items.feedTitle: Feds 'intensely' probing alleged Alaska ballot scheme, US attorney confirms
items.summary: Federal authorities in Alaska are investigating whether Democrat Mary Peltola's campaign violated the law by recruiting a candidate named Dan Sullivan to run in the Senate race against incumbent Republican Dan Sullivan, potentially to confuse voters. The U.S. Attorney for Alaska announced the criminal and civil investigations on Friday. The Department of Justice separately asked a federal judge to isolate ballots ranking Dan J. Sullivan to investigate potential voter confusion.

items.title: Cook Political Report shifts 14 races toward Democrats
items.feedTitle: Cook Political Report shifts 14 races toward Dems ahead of midterms
items.summary: The Cook Political Report moved 14 races toward Democrats ahead of the November midterm elections, as the competitive map has expanded considerably in final days before Election Day. The shift reflects changing dynamics in key battleground races as candidates make final pitches to voters.

items.title: Federal judge signals halt of Trump's monumental arch in DC
items.feedTitle: Federal judge signals she may halt construction on Trump’s arch
items.summary: A federal judge is signaling she may block construction of Trump's proposed 250-foot Triumphal Arch in Washington, D.C., asking whether the desire to rush the project is to 'bedazzle the city.' DOJ attorneys struggled to explain how the arch would protect national security, and several veterans groups have filed objections to the project.

items.title: U.S. approves $2.1 billion Patriot missile sale to Ukraine
items.feedTitle: U.S. approves $2.1 billion sale of Patriot interceptors to Ukraine
items.summary: The State Department approved a possible $2.1 billion sale of 500 Patriot interceptor missiles to Ukraine, funded entirely by U.S. partners. The American-made interceptors are the only effective weapon available for downing Russia's ballistic missiles and represent continued U.S. military support for Ukraine's defense.

items.title: Judge orders Trump administration to hand over noncitizen voter list
items.feedTitle: Judge orders Trump administration to hand over list of alleged noncitizen voters
items.summary: A federal judge ordered the Trump administration to hand over a list of alleged noncitizen voters, rejecting the administration's efforts to suppress California ballots. The court rejected the Justice Department's request to set aside approximately 20,000 disputed ballots pending citizenship verification.

stlouis.title: UMSL program prepares educators for AI-driven future
stlouis.feedTitle: UMSL program helps St. Louis-area educators prepare students for AI-driven future
stlouis.summary: A University of Missouri-St. Louis program is helping St. Louis-area educators prepare students for an AI-driven future, equipping teachers with resources and training to integrate artificial intelligence concepts into their curricula.

stlouis.title: Ashwani Monga named UMSL chancellor
stlouis.feedTitle: University of Missouri names Ashwani Monga as next chancellor of UMSL
stlouis.summary: University of Missouri system names Ashwani Monga as the next chancellor of the University of Missouri-St. Louis, leading the campus into a new chapter of leadership and institutional direction.

stlouis.title: Former Imo's employee dies in Bridgeton shootout
stlouis.feedTitle: Suspect dies in shootout with police at Imo’s Pizza in Bridgeton
stlouis.summary: A former Imo's employee died in a shootout with police at an Imo's location in Bridgeton after holding workers hostage. The suspect was armed and exchanged gunfire with responding officers during the incident.

items.title: G20 cancels group photo as Europe refuses to stand with Lavrov
items.feedTitle: G20 drops group photo as Europeans refuse to stand with Lavrov
items.summary: The U.S. cancelled the traditional G20 'family photo' after Australia, the UK, and approximately one-third of other nations threatened to boycott or walk out in protest of Russia's presence. Secretary of State Marco Rubio pulled the plug after several European officials refused to appear with Russian Foreign Minister Lavrov amid ongoing tensions over Ukraine.

items.title: Iran reports four tankers strike mines in Hormuz Strait
items.feedTitle: Iran says 4 tankers strike mines and catch fire in Strait of Hormuz, and other Mideast news
items.summary: Iran says multiple oil tankers struck mines and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz amid escalating Middle East tensions. The incidents raise concerns about regional stability and maritime security, with oil prices climbing as supply worries intensify.

items.title: Binance suffers record $6.3 billion cryptocurrency hack
items.feedTitle: Crypto giant Binance attempting to recover $6.3bn stolen in hack linked to North Korea
items.summary: Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, says hackers made off with $6.3 billion in assets in what appears to be the largest crypto heist in history. The company halted withdrawals and is working to recover funds, with experts linking the attack to a suspected North Korean hacker group that relies on crypto theft for foreign currency.

items.title: GSLV successfully launches NVS-03 navigation satellite
items.feedTitle: GSLV places next-generation navigation satellite NVS-03 into orbit
items.summary: India's ISRO successfully launched the NVS-03 navigation satellite, strengthening India's indigenous NavIC (Navigation with Indian Constellation) system and improving civilian access to regional satellite navigation. The satellite, with a 12-year mission life, carries an indigenous atomic clock and will restore functioning of the NavIC constellation.

items.title: Helicopter crash kills six near Badrinath pilgrimage site
items.feedTitle: Uttarakhand's Joshimath: Six dead after helicopter crashes in northern Indian state
items.summary: Six people died when a helicopter carrying Badrinath pilgrims crashed in Uttarakhand's Joshimath after taking off Friday afternoon and losing contact. The aircraft was reportedly carrying pilgrims returning from the Hindu pilgrimage site.

items.title: Supreme Court upholds bail for Kashmiri activist Khurram Parvez
items.feedTitle: Supreme Court Dismisses NIA's Plea Challenging Bail Of Kashmiri Activist Khurram Parvez In UAPA Case
items.summary: The Supreme Court dismissed the NIA's plea challenging bail granted to Kashmiri rights activist Khurram Parvez in his UAPA case, upholding his release. The decision marks a legal victory for the activist amid ongoing disputes over charges under India's anti-terror law.

items.title: Census 2027 enumeration to start January 25
items.feedTitle: Census 2027: door-to-door enumeration to start on January 25
items.summary: India's Census 2027 door-to-door enumeration phase will begin on January 25 and conclude by February 28, excluding snow-bound and poll-bound states. The 50-day enumeration period represents a record length for India's decennial census operation.

items.title: India rejects TB drug patent, prioritizing patient access
items.feedTitle: Explained: Why India’s rejection of a TB drug patent matters for patients
items.summary: India's rejection of a tuberculosis drug patent highlights the country's commitment to ensuring patient access to essential medicines while balancing intellectual property concerns. The decision has broader implications for global pharmaceutical policy and treatment availability in developing nations.

immigration.title: US court suspends 2027 Green Card lottery reopening
immigration.feedTitle: US court suspends Green Card lottery for 2027, blocking reopening
immigration.summary: A U.S. court suspended the requirement to hold the 2027 Diversity Visa lottery, blocking its reopening and leaving about 55,000 African applicants uncertain over their prospects for 2027 entry. The Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals stayed the lower court order while litigation continues, leaving the visa program in limbo.

immigration.title: Trump ends H-1B extension protections, finalizes work permit limits
immigration.feedTitle: Trump Administration Moves to End H-1B Extension Protections, Finalizes Restrictions on Work Permit Renewals
immigration.summary: The Trump administration has moved to end H-1B visa extension protections and finalized restrictions on work permit renewals, proposed and not yet final. The changes could affect Indian workers stuck in the green card backlog who rely on H-1B extensions while awaiting employment-based immigration processing.

immigration.title: Texas agriculture department bars H-1B employers from state grants
immigration.feedTitle: Texas agriculture department to bar H-1B employers from some state grants
immigration.summary: Texas's agriculture commissioner has barred businesses employing H-1B visa holders from receiving certain state grants, marking a new restriction on companies using temporary foreign workers. The policy raises stakes for employers and workers in tech and other sectors relying on H-1B sponsorship.

items.title: Nasdaq suffers worst day since June amid AI cash burn fears
items.feedTitle: Stock market rocked as investors dump tech shares; Nasdaq suffers worst day since June
items.summary: Tech stocks plunged on Friday, with the Nasdaq posting its worst day since June as investors shed concerns about mounting debt and negative cash flow undermining the AI spending boom. The sell-off erased over $1 trillion in market value as big tech earnings disappointed and confidence in AI profitability wavered.

items.title: S&P downgrades Meta's outlook on AI spending concerns
items.feedTitle: Meta’s Rating Outlook Cut to Negative by S&P on AI Spending
items.summary: S&P Global cut Meta's rating outlook to negative, citing concerns about cash flow deterioration and capital expenditure pressures from AI investments. The downgrade reflects broader investor anxiety about whether massive AI spending will generate adequate returns.

items.title: Oil giants post record profits as Iran war lifts refining margins
items.feedTitle: ExxonMobil and Chevron report blowout profits as Trump touts benefits of high oil prices
items.summary: ExxonMobil and Chevron reported blowout quarterly profits as Middle East tensions and the Iran war drove up oil and gas prices, boosting refining margins. The companies benefited from regional instability even as Trump highlighted potential economic gains from higher oil prices.

items.title: Federal debt surpasses GDP for first time since WWII
items.feedTitle: Federal debt surpassed GDP for fiscal 2026
items.summary: U.S. federal debt has exceeded the size of the economy for the first time since World War II, reaching 100% of GDP in fiscal 2026. The milestone reflects cumulative budget deficits and raises long-term sustainability questions about government finances.

items.title: Nifty reclaims 23,000 on IT and pharma rally
items.feedTitle: Nifty reclaims 23,000 to end October on a positive note; IT and Pharma lead, midcaps bleed
items.summary: India's Nifty 50 index closed above 23,000 on October 30 as IT and pharma stocks led a recovery, with Sensex gaining 308 points. The rally marks gains for family-sponsored visa categories in the November visa bulletin, though midcaps continued to bleed.

Oil prices rose amid Middle East tensions and Iran war escalation, while gold slipped below $4,000 as the tech rout dominated sentiment. cards.title: The Deep Work Trap
cards.insight: Many knowledge workers equate 'staying busy' with productivity, filling calendars with meetings and reactive tasks that feel important but fragment focus. Real productivity often requires protecting blocks of uninterrupted time, even when there's organizational pressure to be always available.
cards.takeaway: Audit your calendar this week: identify three recurring meetings you can delete or delegate, and defend one 90-minute block for your most important work.

cards.title: Context Switching Debt
cards.insight: Every time you shift between tasks, you incur a cognitive 'cost' that extends far beyond the switch itself. Studies show it can take 15-25 minutes to regain deep focus after an interruption, making frequent task-switching a hidden productivity killer.
cards.takeaway: Batch similar tasks together and turn off notifications during your focus block to minimize the number of context switches you make per day.

cards.title: The Illusion of Multitasking
cards.insight: The human brain doesn't truly multitask; it rapidly switches attention between activities. This creates the feeling of doing more while actually reducing the quality and depth of thought applied to each task.
cards.takeaway: Choose one primary task per work session and treat secondary items as true distractions—not parallel work—to improve output quality.

cards.title: Energy Over Time
cards.insight: Productivity isn't just about time management; it's about managing your mental and physical energy. Peak cognitive performance occurs in 60–90 minute windows, and attempting to sustain focus beyond natural breaks leads to diminishing returns.
cards.takeaway: Identify your peak hours for complex work and schedule your most demanding tasks then; reserve afternoons for routine, lower-stakes activities.

ai.title: Anthropic files record-breaking IPO as valuation soars
ai.summary: Anthropic, the AI startup founded by former OpenAI researchers, has filed for an initial public offering in what could be a record-breaking debut for an AI company. The IPO filing reveals the company's business model and growth trajectory amid the broader AI boom.

ai.title: OpenAI cuts fundraising target by $10 billion
ai.feedTitle: OpenAI cuts funding target by $10 billion, FT reports
ai.summary: OpenAI has slashed its fundraising target by $10 billion amid growing AI spending jitters and investor skepticism about the return on massive infrastructure investments. The cut signals tempering of valuations as questions mount about profitability and cash burn rates.

ai.title: Cracks emerge in the AI spending boom despite continued capex
ai.feedTitle: Cracks are emerging in the AI spending boom
ai.summary: Big Tech companies are pouring billions into AI infrastructure, but mounting debt, negative cash flow, and growing investor skepticism are raising fundamental questions about the sustainability of the AI spending boom. Market turmoil this month has exposed vulnerabilities beneath the surface of AI company valuations.

ai.title: Anthropic's Claude finds critical Linux kernel security bug
ai.feedTitle: Anthropic AI model finds Linux kernel bug that leads to remote root access
ai.summary: Anthropic's AI model Claude discovered a previously unknown Linux kernel vulnerability that could lead to remote root access, demonstrating AI's emerging capability to identify and exploit security flaws. The finding highlights both the power and potential risks of AI-assisted security research.

ai.title: AWS commits to $1 trillion revenue amid record AI capex
ai.feedTitle: AWS will be a $1T business, Jassy says — but first, it will spend big
ai.summary: AWS CEO Andy Jassy says Amazon will become the first $1 trillion revenue business but will continue massive capital expenditure spending to dominate AI cloud computing. The company is betting heavily on being king of the AI infrastructure market despite near-term pressure on margins.
